sections.introduction:
A bad digestion, is the root of all diseases. Without good digestion we can’t even enjoy our meal. There are various factors which are responsible for this problem like lifestyle, improper eating habits, consumption of alcohol and caffeine intake. The bottom line of this article is “Chronic gastritis” which means inflammation on the lining of the stomach. 
 When this inflammation occurs, your stomach lining produces less acid, pepsin, and protective mucus. If you have this condition, you might feel full and heavy after eating just a few bites. Chronic gastritis might be painless or cause dull, persistent stomach pain. Chronic gastritis may lead to stomach bleeding or stomach ulcers and also increases the risk of stomach cancer. So, don’t ignore the symptoms and visit your doctor. 
 With the help of various herbs we can manage the problem of chronic gastritis in a natural way. These are herbs like Amla (Emblica officinalis), Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bahera (Terminalia bellerica), Sounf (Foeniculum vulgare), Jeerak (Cuminum cyminum), Pippali (Piper longum), Dhania (Coriander sativum), Amalaki (Phyllanthus emblica), Gotukola (Centella asiatica) which have cooling effects on body and resolve the problem of chronic gastritis. Though herbs take some time to show their effects but their results are long lasting without any adverse effects on health.
sections.what_is_chronic_gastritis: Chronic gastritis is defined as the inflammation or irritation of the lining of the stomach. The inflammation in gastritis is commonly the result of infection with the same bacterium which is the main cause for most stomach ulcers. The other reason for gastritis are alcohol consumption, caffeine intake, and stress.
sections.symptoms_of_gastritis:
Abdominal pain 
 Loss of appetite 
 Nausea 
 Vomiting 
 Indigestion 
 Black stools 
 Weight loss 
 Bloating and gas 
 Feeling fullness and heaviness in upper abdomen after eating 

 When to See Your Doctor? 
 If stomach irritation persists longer than a week, must visit your doctor.
sections.causes_associated_with_chronic_gastritis:
Use of certain medications like aspirin and ibuprofen. 
 Excessive consumption of alcohol. 
 Certain bacterial infections like Helicobacter pylori which lead to stomach ulcers. 
 Viral infections in weak immunity. 
 Stress. 
 Bile reflux – In this case, there is backflow of bile into the stomach from bile duct.
